commandThreshold_deg.source: JPL news, 'Mars Missions to Pause Commanding in June, Due to Sun' (2015): the moratorium applies while 'the sun will be within two degrees of Mars in Earth's sky'

cycle24.source: NOAA SWPC: Solar Cycle 24 began in December 2008; its smoothed sunspot maximum came in April 2014

cycle25.source: NASA/NOAA: solar minimum Dec. 2019; on Oct. 15, 2024 NASA and NOAA announced the Sun had reached its solar maximum period

length_years.source: NOAA Space Weather Scales: 1 cycle = 11 years. Cycles before 24 and after 25 repeat the nearest cycle's shape every 11 years (game rule).

strongStormsPerCycle.source: NOAA Space Weather Scales: solar radiation storms S3 (strong) 10 per cycle + S4 (severe) 3 per cycle; S5 (fewer than 1 per cycle) not counted. S3 effects include single-event upsets.

quietToActiveRatio.source: Game estimate: storm rate at solar minimum as a fraction of the rate at maximum

distanceExponent.source: Game estimate: storm particle flux taken to fall as 1/r² with distance from the Sun

globalStormsPerMarsYear.source: NASA, 'The Fact and Fiction of Martian Dust Storms': 'Once every three Mars years (about 5 ½ Earth years), on average, normal storms grow into planet-encircling dust storms'

seasonStartLs_deg.source: Season of global storms: southern spring and summer (Ls 180–360°). NASA says larger storms happen in southern summer; the spring start is to verify against NASA source

seasonEndLs_deg.source: End of southern summer (Ls 360°); to verify against NASA source

perihelionLs_deg.source: NASA GISS Mars24 technical notes: areocentric longitude of perihelion L_s,p = 251.000° + 0.0064891° × (yr − 2000)

perihelionLsRate_degPerYear.source: NASA GISS Mars24 technical notes: L_s,p = 251.000° + 0.0064891° × (yr − 2000)

rate_perYear.unit: events per year at the destination
rate_perYear.source: Game estimate: close comet passes or debris streams at a planet are rare

installed.source: Game estimate: four wheels in a pyramid, a common layout

needed.source: Game estimate: three wheels give full three-axis control

weibullShape.source: Game estimate: wear-out failures, hazard rising with age (β > 1)

baseRate_perYear.source: Game estimate: memory upsets that need ground action

stormFactor.source: Game estimate: extra upset rate while a solar storm is active (NOAA S3 lists single-event upsets as likely)

radiationFactor.source: Game estimate: upset rate rises with the radiation dose rate

coldHazardFactor.source: Game estimate: hardware hazard rates on a day with heaters below need

brownoutDaysToLoss.source: Game estimate: days the bus can go unpowered before the craft is lost

capacity_Gbit.source: Game estimate after MRO's solid-state recorder (about 160 Gbit); to verify against NASA source

baseRate_perHour.source: NASA's Mission Operations and Communications Services (JPL D-22674, Oct 2014), Eq. 2-1: R_B contact-dependent hourly rate, $1057/hr for FY09

apertureWeight34.source: NASA MO&CS (Oct 2014), Eq. 2-1: A_W = 1.00 for 34-meter BWG and HEF stations

apertureWeight70.source: NASA MO&CS (Oct 2014), Eq. 2-1: A_W = 4.00 for 70-meter stations

contactsPerWeek.source: Game rule: one pass a day (F_C in NASA MO&CS Eq. 2-1)

passOverhead_h.source: NASA MO&CS (Oct 2014): a 45-minute setup and a 15-minute tear-down are added to each scheduled pass

bookingLead_days.source: Game estimate: DSN passes are scheduled ahead of time

reaction_h.source: Game estimate: time for the operations team to diagnose and prepare a command

cruiseFractions.source: Game estimate: four trajectory-correction burns of equal size

days.source: Game estimate: science paused while the craft recovers from safe mode

optionYears.source: Game rule: one year, or one NASA planetary Senior Review cycle (3 years, to verify against NASA source)

approvalScience.source: Game estimate: stands in for the Senior Review's judgement of science return

inclination_deg.source: Game estimate: a polar mapping orbit
